issue_context.title: OOM when performing inference on an extremely large document with a semantic_text field
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.15.2, 8.16, main

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

linux

### Problem Description

The addition of automatic chunking combined with very large documents has caused some ingest processes to crash, with OOM or quiet restarts of the ML node. 

We are currently working on long-term solutions to this problem which will be released in an upcoming patch.

### Steps to Reproduce

Use semantic_text field to ingest documents over 100k characters in length. 

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_

```
The number of nested documents has exceeded the allowed limit of [10000]
```

This error is usually seen with the ELSER tokens where the field is not mapped as a [sparse_vector](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/sparse-vector.html)
@wwang500, do we know how big the document was that caused this?

> [@wwang500](https://github.com/wwang500), do we know how big the document was that caused this?

The test data I used is 60million chars in one document.

Ok, so 10k chunks at 200 words each is 2M words, at 5 char per word, that would be 10M chars, so by this math it should be impossible to ingest a document with 60M chars with the default settings, and you would need to roughly 6x-10x the default nested documents limit to be able to ingest a document that large. Certainly, I would expect 10xing the default to cause some of the OOM errors that are warned about in the documentation. 

I think this means that the limit for the the maximum document size with chunking is roughly 10MB/10M chars. 

From here, we should probably document this limitation and suggest breaking up documents into roughly 1MB sections before ingesting.

Seeing this cause OOMs again when performing inference with large documents and multiple semantic text fields. Ingesting the rally wikipedia dataset with both an E5 and ELSER dataset has been causing ooms on my project.

> From here, we should probably document this limitation and suggest breaking up documents into roughly 1MB sections before ingesting.

I think we need stronger protection than simply documenting the limitation. We must actively reject work or otherwise bound its resource usage before it causes harm to the cluster (e.g. by failing a node).
